target_customer: Solo writers, bloggers and small writing teams, plus buyers of an editing service
problem: Autosaving word processors clutter history with versions. Draft saved named drafts with version control, collaboration and an editor marketplace.
business_model: Free app with an editing service sold to bloggers and organizations without copy editors
product_category: Online word processor with version control

founders.name: Nathan Kontny
founders.background_notes: YC page: sole founder; a Hacker News profile for nate says he ran Highrise, which was not opened as a source on the page. Education not listed.

exit.reason: No reason stated; Draft stopped new sign-ups and closed at the end of 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: A web editor with version diffing and import from Dropbox and Evernote built by one person is modest engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Google Docs and other editors could add named versions easily and Draft had no network or data moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in March 2013 positioned Draft against Google Docs autosave and Word; no incumbent acquired or copied it according to sources found.

market_need_then: A March 2013 TechCrunch review argued Google Docs autosave clutters history and Word is heavy; no evidence dated near the 2011 batch was found.

identity.visual_style: Minimal interface with large plain text on a light gray background; a mark draft button; red and green edits (TechCrunch March 2013)

branding.brand_signature: Mark draft button that saves a named stage of writing
branding.community_and_virality: Reviewed by TechCrunch, Engadget, ProfHacker and The Write Life in 2013; Beeminder had an integration

brand_strength.rationale: Good review coverage but a generic word name shared with many products, so search confusion was likely.

outcome_analysis: Draft was a one-person product that launched publicly in March 2013 and stayed small, with no funding found. It disabled sign-ups and closed at the end of 2022 without a stated reason, per Beeminder pages. The failure factors are inferences from a free tool competing against Google Docs with only a niche editing service for revenue.
notes: Competitors left empty: the only dated sources are from 2013, two years after the Summer 2011 batch. Public launch was March 2013 per TechCrunch. Seedtable lists no funding. Shutdown rests on Beeminder help and forum pages, not a Draft announcement. draftin.com does not resolve from this environment.
